adds.title: Doe et al. v. Ventura et al. (2001)
adds.summary: On May 15, 2001, Minn. Stat. 609.293, which punished voluntarily engaging in or submitting to sodomy defined as carnally knowing any person by the anus or by or with the mouth with up to one year imprisonment and/or up to a $3,000 fine, was declared unconstitutional as applied to private, consensual, non-commercial acts of sodomy by consenting adults as violating the right of privacy guaranteed by the Minnesota Constitution.

adds.title: House File 146 - 'Trans Refuge Bill' and March 2023 Executive Order
adds.summary: On March 24, 2023 the Minnesota House passed House File 146 by 68-62 to protect transgender patients from other states and providers of gender-affirming care that is legal in Minnesota from legal action in states where such care is banned or restricted, prohibiting enforcement in Minnesota of out-of-state subpoenas, arrest warrants and extradition requests related to such care and barring compliance with out-of-state court orders to remove children from parental custody for obtaining such care, with Governor Tim Walz having signed an executive order protecting gender-affirming care and intending to sign the bill into law upon Senate passage after it cleared its final Senate committee.
